prompt.context_jp: 夕暮れの陸上部の練習場に、乾いた怒声___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕暮れの陸上部の練習場に、乾いた怒声___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the angry voice as new information in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: This is the opening sentence — the 'angry voice' is brand-new information being introduced into the narrative, so が is used.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the voice as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit a scene-opening description. を is wrong because 響く is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: A voice rang out (new to scene).

prompt.context_jp: 故障を抱えたまま復帰を急ぐ彼にとって、この一対の脚だけ___すべての拠り所であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: この一対の脚だけ___すべての拠り所であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that fits with 'only this pair of legs' as the exhaustive sole support.

feedback.correct_en: だけが marks exhaustive listing — 'these legs and nothing else' are his entire basis. が highlights the uniqueness.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would contrast legs with other things he still has, softening the exclusivity. に doesn't fit the subject role here.

prompt.context_jp: 毛塚___今、メディアが最も取り上げたい新星として業界を席巻しつつあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 毛塚___今、メディアが最も取り上げたい新星として業界を席巻しつつあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking Kezuka as the established topic of this paragraph.

feedback.correct_en: Kezuka was just introduced in the previous sentence and is now the topic being described, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce him as new info, which clashes since he was just mentioned. を doesn't fit as a subject marker.

prompt.context_jp: 先輩たち___軽い口調で発破をかけたが、その言葉の底には遠慮のような気遣いがにじんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先輩たち___軽い口調で発破をかけたが…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the seniors' as the sentence's topic in this contrastive clause?

feedback.correct_en: は sets up 'the seniors' as topic and sets up the が contrast ('they encouraged him, BUT underneath...').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it feel like a sudden identification rather than a topical description about a known group.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は笑ったが、目は冷たかった。
contrast_examples.en: He laughed, but his eyes were cold.

prompt.context_jp: 食事の途中、茂木の携帯電話___短く鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茂木の携帯電話___短く鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces the ringing phone as a sudden new event.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden, new event ('his phone rang') is prototypical new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the phone was already the topic, which doesn't match the surprise of an incoming call during dinner.

prompt.context_jp: 電話口の言葉___柔らかいが、その奥にある結論___ほとんど動かしがたいものであるらしい。
prompt.prompt_jp: 電話口の言葉___柔らかいが、その奥にある結論___ほとんど動かしがたい…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the pair of particles for this contrastive sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Both slots use contrastive は: the words ARE soft, BUT the conclusion IS unmovable. The two は's set up the explicit contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in either slot would mark new information rather than two contrasting known elements being compared.

contrast_examples.jp: 外は寒いが、中は暖かい。
contrast_examples.en: Outside is cold but inside is warm.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺じゃ ___ないってことですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「俺じゃ ___ないってことですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Mogi suspects he isn't a worthy match for Kezuka. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 釣り合う means 'to be a match/balanced with' — exactly Mogi's self-deprecating reading of being paired with the star Kezuka.
feedback.incorrect_en: 間に合う = 'be in time'. 似合う = 'suit/look good on' (clothes etc.), not about parity of status.

contrast_examples.en: The two aren't an even match.

prompt.context_jp: 「そのことなんですが… 今回は ___ ということになりまして」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今回は ___ ということになりまして」
prompt.prompt_en: The reporter is politely cancelling. Which word is the standard business euphemism?

feedback.correct_en: 見送り is the set business euphemism for 'passing on / declining this time'. The nominal form fits ...ということになる.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見直し means 'review/revise', not cancel. 見送る (verb) doesn't fit grammatically before ということになりまして.

contrast_examples.jp: 今回は見送らせていただきます。
計画の見直しが必要だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「毛塚選手との ___ がつかなくて」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「毛塚選手との ___ がつかなくて」
prompt.prompt_en: The reporter couldn't get Kezuka to agree. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 折り合いがつく = 'reach an agreement/compromise'. The negative here means they couldn't come to terms with Kezuka.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕上がり = finish/completion. 打ち合わせ = a meeting; it doesn't collocate with がつく this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 条件の折り合いがつかない。

prompt.context_jp: 扉を開ければ、電気もつけずに机の前で顔を伏せる大地の背中___あった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大地の背中___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that presents Daichi's back as the newly perceived scene.

feedback.correct_en: Visual discovery / existence sentences with ある/いる take が: the father opens the door and 'there is Daichi's back'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make his back an already-established topic, which contradicts the moment-of-discovery framing.

prompt.context_jp: 「飯山さん___ “必ずできる”って言ったんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「飯山さん___ “必ずできる”って言ったんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: The father is reporting what Iiyama (a known person) said. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Iiyama is the known topic of the ongoing conversation; は naturally marks him as 'as for Iiyama, he said...'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would emphasize 'it was Iiyama (not someone else) who said it,' which doesn't match the father's calm appeal.

contrast_examples.en: Dad is the one who came home!

prompt.context_jp: 「もし そうだったとしても “___”ってのも あるんじゃないんか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「“___”ってのも あるんじゃないんか」
prompt.prompt_en: The father quotes a Japanese proverb. Which phrase fits?

feedback.correct_en: ウソから出た誠 = 'truth born from a lie' — a lie that ends up becoming real. The father later echoes it in sentence 166.
feedback.incorrect_en: ウソも方便 means 'a lie is sometimes expedient'. ウソ八百 means 'a pack of lies'. Neither matches 'turning out to be true'.

contrast_examples.en: The lie turned out to be true.

prompt.context_jp: 「あれ___ ウソをついてる人間に見えるか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あれ___ ウソをついてる人間に見えるか？」
prompt.prompt_en: The father points to Iiyama's back and challenges Daichi. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The father is pointing out something visible and asking 'does THAT look like a liar?' — using が for the newly pointed-at referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the dramatic 'look at THAT!' feel; it would sound more like generic commentary.

prompt.context_jp: 「何かから逃げ出して飲む酒は ___ んだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「何かから逃げ出して飲む酒は ___ んだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Iiyama tells Daichi how escapist drinking tastes.

feedback.correct_en: The whole point is contrast with the good sake he's saving for success — escape-drinking is まずい ('tastes bad').
feedback.incorrect_en: うまい is the opposite. ぬるい ('lukewarm') is literal temperature and doesn't fit this emotional contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 逃げて飲む酒はまずい。

prompt.context_jp: 翌朝、こはぜ屋の事務所で電話___鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: こはぜ屋の事務所で電話___鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle introducing the ringing phone as a new scene event.

feedback.correct_en: A new event in a scene-setting line: 'a phone rang' — classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the phone as a pre-established topic, which doesn't match a fresh scene opening.

contrast_examples.jp: そのドアは開いていた。

prompt.context_jp: 有村が伝えたのは、茂木裕人___陸王を試し履きしてくれているらしいという情報である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茂木裕人___陸王を試し履きしてくれているらしい…
prompt.prompt_en: Inside the embedded clause reporting new information, which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate clause reporting a newly discovered fact, が marks the subject naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside such 'the information that X' clauses sounds unnatural because the embedded subject isn't a topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「コーヒーは 温度によって味が ___ んですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「コーヒーは 温度によって味が ___ んですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Yasuda explains that flavor shifts with temperature.

feedback.correct_en: 味が変わる = 'the flavor changes' (intransitive). The subject 味 pairs with intransitive 変わる.
feedback.incorrect_en: 変える is transitive ('to change something') and needs を. 替わる means 'be replaced' (one thing swapped for another), not 'shift gradually'.

prompt.context_jp: 「一流の職人が 最後に ___ のは勘ですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「一流の職人が 最後に ___ のは勘ですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb for 'what a master craftsman ultimately relies on'.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に頼る = 'to rely on'. 勘に頼る is the standard phrase for falling back on intuition.
feedback.incorrect_en: 預ける = 'entrust/deposit'. 任せる = 'leave it to someone'. Neither captures 'relying on gut' as a last resort.

contrast_examples.en: In the end, you rely on gut.
To leave the work to someone.

prompt.context_jp: 「煮繭温度___変われば 硬さ___変わるってことが分かったぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「煮繭温度___変われば 硬さ___変わる…」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particles for this conditional discovery.

feedback.correct_en: Conditional subordinate clauses with ば typically take が for the subject. 硬さも ('hardness too') expresses the parallel change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は in both ば-clauses sounds unnatural for a cause-effect statement. を is wrong — 変わる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: 温度が変われば味も変わる。
contrast_examples.en: If the temperature changes, the taste changes too.

prompt.context_jp: 「企業規模で___ アトランティスには 到底 勝てませんが コンセプトに___自信があります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「企業規模で___ アトランティスには…勝てませんが コンセプトに___自信があります」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particles for this classic contrastive 'in X we can't win, but in Y we're confident'.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は on both sides sharpens the pair: 'as for scale (we lose), but as for concept (we're confident)'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't attach contrastively here, and も would mean 'also/even', missing the opposition.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段は高いが、味は良い。
contrast_examples.en: The price is high, but the taste is good.
Both price and taste are good.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が仲間を鼓舞する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a motivational shout in this scene?

choices.text: 今日は縁起がいい 大丈夫だ 絶対に うまくいく！
今日が縁起はいい 大丈夫だ 絶対に うまくいく！

feedback.correct_en: Topic-comment 今日は with 縁起がいい inside is the standard pattern: 'as for today, luck is good.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 今日が縁起は… reverses the roles and sounds broken — 縁起がいい is a fixed collocation, not something you split with は.

prompt.context_jp: 茂木が宮沢の靴を評価する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural when giving a polite but critical professional assessment?

choices.text: レース用としては厳しいですね
レース用としては難しいをしますね

feedback.correct_en: 〜としては厳しい is a set softened-negative evaluation phrase ('it's a tough sell for X use').
feedback.incorrect_en: '難しいをします' is ungrammatical — 難しい is an い-adjective and can't take を to form a verb.

contrast_examples.jp: プロの基準では厳しい。

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が頭を下げて頼み込む場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which plea sounds more natural in this earnest business context?

choices.text: 私たちに あなたのサポートを させてください
私たちは あなたのサポートが してあげたいです

feedback.correct_en: 〜させてください is the standard humble request to be allowed to do something — perfect for a town-factory boss asking a star athlete.
feedback.incorrect_en: してあげたい sounds condescending ('I want to do you the favor of...') and awkward with サポートが — the particle doesn't fit the verb.

prompt.context_jp: 試作が成功した瞬間の歓声。
prompt.prompt_en: Which spontaneous exclamation sounds more natural at the moment of breakthrough?

choices.text: できましたのだ！ できましたのだ！

feedback.correct_en: Plain できた! is the natural burst of joy in a workshop among coworkers.
feedback.incorrect_en: できましたのだ! mixes polite past with のだ in a way that's stiff and ungrammatical for a spontaneous shout.

prompt.context_jp: 「ソール___ どう変わろうと こんな 素人が作った シューズをお前が履く必要はない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ソール___ どう変わろうと…」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'as for the soles, no matter how they change'.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜ようと concessive clause, が typically marks the subject of the inner verb (ソールが変わる).
feedback.incorrect_en: は in this concessive subordinate clause sounds unnatural; concessive subject clauses prefer が.

contrast_examples.jp: 何が起ころうと平気だ。
contrast_examples.en: No matter what happens, I'm fine.

prompt.context_jp: 協力を申し出る丁寧な場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which offer of help sounds more natural and appropriately polite?

choices.text: その夢 私にも 手伝わせてもらえないだろうか
その夢 私も 手伝ってやろうじゃないか

feedback.correct_en: 手伝わせてもらえないだろうか is a humble, deferential way to offer help — appropriate when approaching someone's cherished dream.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手伝ってやろうじゃないか is boastful/condescending ('I'll do you the favor'), clashing with the respectful tone needed here.

contrast_examples.jp: 参加させていただけませんか。
contrast_examples.en: May I be allowed to join?
